description: Extend run_benchmark_bedrock.py to support all 10 target models and all 29 benchmarks across 5 tracks
steps: Step 1: Read repo/scripts/run_benchmark_bedrock.py fully to understand the existing single-model metacog-only Bedrock runner architecture

Step 2: Add a MODEL_CATALOG dict mapping all 10 model IDs from GOALS.md (anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1, deepseek.r1-v1:0, openai.gpt-oss-120b-1:0, deepseek.v3.2, qwen.qwen3-next-80b-a3b, amazon.nova-pro-v1:0, meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0, anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0, zai.glm-4.7, mistral.ministral-3-3b-instruct) with friendly labels
Step 3: Import the full BENCHMARKS dict from run_benchmark_local.py (all 5 tracks, 29 benchmarks) into the Bedrock runner, or refactor both to share a common benchmark registry

Step 4: Add --model CLI arg accepting model ID or friendly name, defaulting to claude-sonnet-4; add --track arg to filter by track (metacognition, learning, attention, executive_functions, social_cognition, all)
Step 5: Add retry logic (3 retries with exponential backoff starting at 5s) and timeout handling (120s per benchmark call) to create_bedrock_llm()
Step 6: Add rate limiting: 2s delay between benchmark runs, 5s delay between models to avoid Bedrock throttling
Step 7: Output per-model results to results/{model_id}.json with schema {model, model_label, timestamp, scores: {benchmark_name: {score, error, duration_s}}}
Step 8: Test the runner with --model anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 --benchmark metacog_canary (cheapest model, single benchmark) to verify it works end-to-end

description: Run all 29 benchmarks against all 10 Bedrock models and produce score_matrix.csv
steps: Step 1: Run --model mistral.ministral-3-3b-instruct --benchmark all --output results/mistral.ministral-3-3b-instruct.json as smoke test (cheapest model)
Step 2: Run benchmarks for remaining 9 models sequentially, outputting results/{model_id}.json for each
Step 3: If a model fails on a specific benchmark, log error in JSON with score=null and error message, do not abort
Step 4: After all 10 models complete, verify all 10 result files exist in results/ with 29 benchmark entries each
Step 5: Write a Python script to merge all 10 JSON files into results/score_matrix.csv (rows=29 benchmarks, columns=10 models, cells=scores or ERROR)

description: Perform discriminatory power analysis on score_matrix.csv and write results/discriminatory_analysis.md
steps: Step 1: Load results/score_matrix.csv into pandas DataFrame
Step 2: For each benchmark row compute: mean, std, min, max, range across 10 models
Step 3: Flag benchmarks where all models score > 0.9 (too easy), all < 0.1 (too hard), or std < 0.05 (non-discriminatory)
Step 4: Compute discrimination index = score(Claude Opus) - score(Ministral 3B) for each benchmark
Step 5: Rank benchmarks by discrimination index
Step 6: Write results/discriminatory_analysis.md with: full score matrix table, per-benchmark stats, flagged benchmarks with reasons, discrimination ranking, fix recommendations

description: Fix non-discriminatory metacognition benchmarks identified in discriminatory_analysis.md
steps: Step 1: Read results/discriminatory_analysis.md to identify flagged metacognition benchmarks
Step 2: For each flagged benchmark, analyze per-model scores to diagnose why discrimination is low (ceiling, floor, or scoring bug)
Step 3: Implement fixes in repo/benchmarks/metacognition/ source files (add harder/easier items, adjust scoring, add sub-tasks)
Step 4: Re-test each fixed benchmark against 3 models (Claude Opus=strongest, Nova Pro=mid, Ministral 3B=weakest) via run_benchmark_bedrock.py
Step 5: Verify fix improved discrimination: std across 3 models > 0.10 and range > 0.20
Step 6: Update corresponding Kaggle notebooks in repo/notebooks/ to match fixed source code

description: Update SUBMISSION_NARRATIVE.md and KAGGLE_DISCUSSION_DRAFT.md with cross-model discriminatory power results
steps: Step 1: Read results/discriminatory_analysis.md and results/score_matrix.csv
Step 2: In SUBMISSION_NARRATIVE.md add/update Cross-Model Discriminatory Power Analysis section with score matrix table, key discrimination findings, three-tier metacognition pattern across models
Step 3: Replace placeholder scores in per-track sections with actual model scores
Step 4: In KAGGLE_DISCUSSION_DRAFT.md add results highlights (calibration failure pattern, three-tier metacognition, best-discriminating benchmarks)
Step 5: Update IAN_TODO.md with any new action items (re-upload fixed notebooks, re-register CB tasks)
